quests.title: End to End
quests.summary: Get an End to End card stamped at both ends of Britain, 874 miles apart.

steps.text: Take your End to End card to the Land's End end: find the End to Ender in Penzance and win your stamp.
Bring the stamped card back to the End to End Clerk at the John o' Groats signpost.

quests.reward: An End to End Certificate, a lucky Groatie Buckie and Scottish standing.

quests.title: The Bog Survey
quests.summary: Help the Forsinard warden survey the Flow Country, Europe's greatest blanket bog.

steps.text: Count the dubh lochans with the Flowmoor by the pools on the Dubh Lochan Trail.
Listen for the greenshank with the bird surveyor at the south end of the trail.
Help the peat scientist west of the road take a peat core, once your team has proved it won't sink.
Report back to the Flows Warden at the Forsinard visitor centre.

quests.reward: A Bog Myrtle Sprig charm, crowdie oatcakes and Scottish standing.

quests.title: Crossing the Pentland Firth
quests.summary: Fetch tide tables, cross the Firth to Orkney and face what walks out of the sea off Duncansby.

steps.text: Win the Tide Watcher's tide tables at the Merry Men of Mey, east of Thurso.
Sail from Scrabster to Orkney and give the tide tables to the Pentland Skipper on the Kirkwall quay.
After dark, on the sands below Duncansby Head, face the Nuckelavee and catch it.
Tell Skipper Morag on the Scrabster quay.

quests.reward: A Burn Water Flask charm, partan bree and Scottish standing (and a Nuckelavee).

quests.title: The Castle of Mey Garden
quests.summary: Feed the Queen Mother's walled garden with seaweed from the shore and peat from the bog.

steps.text: Fetch a creel of seaweed from the gatherer on Dunnet Bay.
Bring a bag of peat from the peat cutter in the Flow Country.
Take both back to the Head Gardener in the walled garden at Mey.

quests.reward: Caithness flagstones, heather honey, crowdie oatcakes and Scottish standing.
